_comment: Permission grant for the unattended 07:00 daily-triage run (.github/workflows/scheduled-tasks.yml).
Passed with `claude --settings`, which MERGES with the host's settings rather than replacing them.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS, AND WHY IT IS NOT `--dangerously-skip-permissions`:
A non-interactive `claude -p` session gets a sandbox scoped to the runner workspace and no tool
grants, so the 2026-08-05 run reached the model and correctly refused to do anything: it could
not read $HOME/life, could not run gh, and was denied the Drive connector. The obvious fix is to
bypass permission checks entirely. #203 argues against exactly that, for exactly this context —
'Mission Control dispatches are remote and unattended, which is precisely the context where
skipping the permission prompt has the largest blast radius' — and says it needs its own issue
and an explicit opt-in rather than being added quietly while replacing something else. So this
is an allowlist, in git, reviewable in a diff.
THE DENY LIST IS THE POINT. skills/daily-triage/SKILL.md opens with 'Hard limits — read before
anything else': draft PRs only, never merge, never mark ready-for-review, never push to main,
never send mail, never touch the calendar, nothing destructive. Those were prose in a prompt —
instructions the model is asked to follow, with nothing stopping it. Deny rules take precedence
over allow, so the most dangerous of them are now actually enforced by the harness. That is the
difference between a control that reads as enforced and one that can fire.
Denials are deliberately narrow: they block the specific irreversible or outward-facing action,
not the whole tool. `gh` stays usable for the GitHub sweep and for opening draft PRs; only merge
and ready-for-review are blocked. Gmail stays readable and can draft; it cannot send.
